title: A Provision for the Passage
premise: Petra Oyelaran, a desert ranger who has spent nine years outrunning a warrant from his old garrison, is hired to track a thief who stole nothing but a map. The trail ends at a riverbank where floodwater has exposed a sealed chest bearing the crest of Kessarine, a nation erased from every atlas. The expedition that claims the chest — led by the magistrate's daughter, Ilse Varn — needs a guide who can cross the salt flats before the dry season seals them, and Petra is the only one who knows the way. As rival claimants, his own former commander, and the thief himself converge on the route home, Petra must decide whether loyalty to the people depending on him matters more than the truth about what Kessarine was and why his own name appears in its records. He brings the expedition home by burning the chest's contents and testifying to what he saw, trading his anonymity for justice outside any court.
about_author: Theo Oyelaran is a former surveyor for boundary commissions who walked the salt corridors of three countries before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels in which landscapes keep better records than governments do.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stole Nothing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A frontier clerk hires him to recover a stolen map, insisting nothing else was taken. Petra reads the theft as deliberate: the thief left coin behind. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking the restlessness of a man who cannot afford to be found.

chapters.title: Tracks in Salt
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Three days across hardpan following a tracker smarter than the client claimed, reading water caches and deliberate misdirection. The thief wants to be followed — slowly. Emotional beat: grudging respect curdling into suspicion that he is someone's instrument.

chapters.title: What the River Gave Back
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the flooded riverbend he finds the thief dead — not murdered, drowned — and beside him a bronze-bound chest stamped with the seal of Kessarine. Emotional beat: dread; Petra recognizes the seal from a childhood story his mother told and immediately regrets knowing it.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ilse Varn's POV. She arrives with an armed expedition and papers claiming salvage rights, offering Petra triple pay to guide them home before the dry season. She lies smoothly about what the chest contains. Emotional beat: Ilse's controlled ambition, and her first flicker of doubt about her father's orders.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Not Being Found
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback-woven. He accepts the job because refusing means explaining himself, and his name is on a garrison warrant for a fire he did or didn't set. Emotional beat: the cost of stopping made concrete — memory as a debt that compounds.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dead Nation
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Night inventory: records, a ledger of names, and a sealed annex her father explicitly ordered returned unopened. One name in the ledger stops her cold — Oyelaran. Emotional beat: temptation; she pockets one page and tells no one.

chapters.title: The Company of Strangers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The expedition fractures on the first march: a cartographer who asks too many questions, guards loyal to Varn's money, a young archivist named Sef who befriends Petra. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging; Petra catches himself caring whether they survive.

chapters.title: Water Is a Verdict
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A miscalculated well forces rationing; a guard hoards and Petra enforces desert law outside any statute — the group votes, the guard is bound and left with a marked cache. Emotional beat: justice without law working, and terrifying Petra with how easily it could not.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Spotters see a second party shadowing them — garrison cavalry under Commander Hale, the man holding Petra's warrant. Sef realizes his friend is running from something. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by curiosity; Sef chooses silence, for now.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She opens the annex against orders: testimony that Kessarine was dismantled deliberately, its people dispersed by treaty fraud, and her father's office signed the dispersal order. Emotional beat: vertigo — the truth she carries indicts the man funding her future.

chapters.title: Hale at the Ford
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Hale intercepts them at a river ford, offers Petra amnesty for the chest. Petra refuses without explaining why, and the refusal costs the expedition a day and a wounded guard. Emotional beat: the past arriving with paperwork; Petra's loyalty shifting from self-preservation to the people behind him.

chapters.title: Sef Reads the Page
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Ilse's stolen page surfaces; Sef matches the handwriting in the ledger to entries naming Petra's family among the dispersed. He confronts Petra privately. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted — the secret makes Petra more legible, not less, and their friendship deepens through it.

chapters.title: The Salt Corridor
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The only route home crosses flats that will become impassable in six days. Petra commits the expedition to a night march he alone can navigate, making himself indispensable and unfireable. Emotional beat: purpose; for once moving forward and staying hidden are the same direction.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A salt storm scatters the column; Ilse and Petra shelter together and she reveals half the annex's contents, testing him. He reveals the warrant. Emotional beat: two liars trading partial truths and finding each other almost trustworthy.

chapters.title: The Thief's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Among the dead thief's effects, a letter: he was Kessarine's last record-keeper's grandson, and he stole the map to force someone — anyone — to find the chest. Emotional beat: grief reframing the whole journey; the 'crime' was a summons.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Circle
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Hale corners the column at a canyon mouth with overwhelming numbers and a new offer: the chest for everyone's freedom except Petra's. The expedition must choose. Emotional beat: the group, forged by the desert, refuses to trade him — loyalty repaid.

chapters.title: The Ledger Speaks
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. To break the standoff, Ilse reads the annex aloud to both parties: her father's signature, the dispersal order, the manufactured famine. Hale's soldiers waver. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon sharper than the cavalry's; the law's men confronted with the law's crime.

chapters.title: Fire on the Flats
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the chaos, Hale moves to seize the chest by force; Petra burns it and the ledger rather than let either side own the past — keeping only the pages naming the dispersed families, which he distributes. Emotional beat: climax; destruction as preservation, and Petra finally choosing what his name means.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Unread
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Aftermath of the fight: Hale retreats rather than massacre witnesses to testimony already spoken aloud; two guards defect to escort the expedition home. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; the truth, once voiced, cannot be repossessed.

chapters.title: Home Before the Dry Season
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The expedition reaches the river town as wells run low. Ilse files her father's signature with a frontier tribunal that operates outside imperial courts, disowning her inheritance. Emotional beat: costly integrity; she loses her name's protection and gains her own.

chapters.title: The Warrant, Answered
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra surrenders to a civilian magistrate instead of Hale, telling the whole story of the garrison fire — which he set, to destroy the local copy of the dispersal order, at his mother's dying request. The tribunal voids the warrant. Emotional beat: nine years of flight ending in voluntary stillness; memory discharged like a debt paid in full.

chapters.title: A Provision for the Passage
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, closing. He guides one last small caravan — Sef, Ilse, and the defected guards carrying copies of the family names toward the scattered descendant towns. He stops when he chooses now. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the passage provisioned not by secrecy but by shared, survivable truth.
